counterfactual_missing_items: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging was indicated but not performed because of chronic kidney disease and patient preference.
A septal endomyocardial biopsy was considered but deferred due to its low yield.
decisive_items: Based on an epsilon wave in V1–V3, T-wave inversions in V1–V3 with QRS >110 ms, an RV outflow tract dimension >32 mm, and severe RV dilation and hypokinesia, arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia was highly suspected
a markedly dilated right ventricle with severely reduced systolic function
response.rationale: R1 is directly supported by the explicit diagnostic conclusion and multiple ARVD criteria (epsilon wave, TWI, RVOT dilation, severe RV hypokinesia). C1 is an append-only completion whose added RV systolic dysfunction is already contained in R1's raw support, so it is a correlated restatement. R2 rests only on a differential-diagnosis mention and lacks ARVD-specific or sarcoid-specific confirmatory findings.

rejected.why: Only a differential-diagnosis mention triggered by pulmonary nodules; no sarcoid-specific raw findings such as granulomas, MRI, or biopsy support, while ARVD is explicitly 'highly suspected'.
